content:
Apple and the European Union's long-running antitrust dispute over iPhone app sales appears to have finally come to an end.

The EU has welcomed Apple's new app commission fee structure in the region. Under the revised terms, developers will pay commissions or fees ranging from 5% to 26%, depending on their revenue and chosen sales channels...

EU legislation required Apple to allow third-party app stores to operate. While Apple has complied, it faced complaints over the commissions and fees it charges for third-party sales.

Apple has fully introduced the new terms this week, and the EU side appears satisfied with this.

  • Apps selling digital goods and services through Apple's in-app purchase system will face a commission rate of 26%. For the vast majority of developers—including those in the App Store Small Business Programme, Mini Apps Partner Programme, or Video Partner Programme, as well as subscriptions that automatically renew after the first year—the commission rate is 15%.
  • App Store apps using alternative payment processing will face a commission rate of 20%. Developers in the aforementioned programmes can enjoy a reduced rate of 10%.
  • App Store apps that complete purchases via external links within the app will face a commission rate of 15%. Developers in the aforementioned programmes can similarly enjoy a reduced rate of 10%.
  • Apps distributed via alternative app marketplaces or the web will be subject to a 5% "Core Technology Fee" charged by Apple.

The European Commission told the Irish Independent it welcomes the new terms.

A spokesperson said: "The Commission welcomes the adjustments Apple has made to its commercial terms. Following the Commission's non-compliance decision on Apple's steering terms in April 2025 and its preliminary findings on alternative app distribution, the two sides have engaged in close dialogue, which has led to today's revised terms. With today's announcement of the new arrangements, the Commission will monitor Apple's effective implementation of the new terms."

9to5Mac Take

This long-running dispute appears to have finally been resolved. The situation in the United States, however, is a different story. The latest development is that Apple is seeking settlement talks with Epic Games, but the game developer believes this will not yield substantive results. The court will determine the next steps.
